userMessages.text:
# Canary delivery with automatic rollback

Our delivery platform starts when a protected branch produces a signed source revision. The pipeline coordinator runs dependency installation, compilation, unit tests, integration tests, a software-composition scan, and an image vulnerability scan. Successful builds publish an immutable image and provenance statement to the registry. Failures stop the revision and notify its owner with the failed gate.

The release manager promotes the same image into a staging environment, runs database compatibility checks before migration, applies backward-compatible migrations, deploys the services, and executes smoke and contract tests. A failed staging check stops promotion and preserves staging logs and artifacts. Production promotion requires an approved change record and uses a canary controller to send five percent of traffic to the new revision.

The canary controller evaluates error rate, latency, saturation, and a business success metric over consecutive observation windows. Healthy windows increase traffic to twenty-five, fifty, and one hundred percent. A breached threshold freezes further rollout and triggers rollback to the last known-good image; the migration controller runs a compensating action only when the migration declared one safe. The traffic router, feature-flag service, and service registry must agree on the active revision. Rollout state, approvals, metric decisions, traffic changes, and rollback actions enter an audit log, and operators receive notifications at every promotion, pause, failure, and recovery.

If metric telemetry is unavailable, the rollout pauses for operator review instead of assuming success. An operator may resume after telemetry recovers or order a rollback, but cannot bypass failed security gates or image-signature verification.
